verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300-dpi render of PDF page 937 (printed page 913, informative index) against page-937.md. Every index term and every page number on the page is present in the markdown, in the printed order: the left column (Sequential 177 through FLOAT-DECIMAL-16 / Definition 409) and the right column (FLOAT-DECIMAL-16 phrase, USAGE clause, FLOAT-DECIMAL-34 phrase, USAGE clause 405, FLOAT-DECIMAL-34 / Definition 409 ... FRACTION-PART function 673). The PDF does print the odd three-level nesting the claim quotes (FLOAT-DECIMAL-16 phrase > USAGE clause > FLOAT-DECIMAL-34 phrase > USAGE clause 405), and the markdown keeps exactly those words, joining the first two onto one line and marking the last with  . The only difference is indentation and line joining, which is layout of an informative index; no word, term or page reference is missing, added, misattributed or reordered. The cited ambiguity is not real in practice either: the sub-entry 'FLAG-85 directive 57' and the headword 'FLAG-85 directive 55, 57' carry different locators and both stay in place. Under the brief's rejection criteria (formatting/line wrapping only, no change of content), this is not a content discrepancy.
